title: GA-NIFS: JWST/NIRSpec IFS view of the z ∼ 3.5 galaxy GS5001 and its close environment at the core of a large-scale overdensity
question: Characterise the spatially resolved physical and kinematic properties of the ionised gas and interstellar medium in the z=3.47 galaxy GS5001 and its close companions at the core of a candidate protocluster.

what.value: Stellar masses and star formation rates of GS5001 and GS4921 from SED fitting

evidence.quote: GS5001 has a star formation rate (SFR) in the range 150-240 M⊙ yr−1 (Troncoso et al. 2014; Pacifici et al. 2016; Pérez-González et al. 2005; Guo et al. 2013)
The southern companion, GS4921, has SFR = 35 − 70 M⊙ yr−1 and stellar mass M⋆ = 0.5 − 2.3 × 1010 M⊙ (Maiolino et al. 2008; Pérez-González et al. 2005; Guo et al. 2013).

external_data.citation: Troncoso et al. 2014; Pacifici et al. 2016; Pérez-González et al. 2005; Guo et al. 2013; Maiolino et al. 2008; Santini et al. 2015

what.value: X-ray luminosity of GS5001 L0.5−7 keV = 9.5 × 1042 erg s−1

evidence.quote: GS5001 is also detected in the X-ray, although with a small number of counts (20 counts), and has an aperture corrected X-ray luminosity of L0.5−7 keV = 9.5 × 1042 erg s−1 (Fiore et al. 2012; Luo et al. 2017).

external_data.citation: Fiore et al. 2012; Luo et al. 2017

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST/NIRSpec IFS data cubes and register astrometry
recipe.method: Reduce raw NIRSpec R2700 and R100 data with modified JWST pipeline v1.8.2, drizzle to 0.05 arcsec spaxels, rescale noise vectors, and align astrometry to HST/WFC3 F125W and Gaia DR3.
key_parameters: spaxel size 0.05 arcsec; error rescaling median factor 1.6

recipe.goal: Image ALMA CO(4-3) data cube and create moment 0 map
recipe.method: Image calibrated ALMA MS in CASA tclean with natural weighting, bin spectral channels to ~10 km s^-1, and integrate continuum-subtracted cube within ±800 km s^-1 of CO(4-3) at z=3.47.
key_parameters: natural weighting; spectral binning to ~10 km s^-1; integration window ±800 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Fit optical emission lines spaxel-by-spaxel and in integrated apertures
recipe.method: Subtract continuum with Savitzky-Golay filter and simultaneously fit optical emission lines in R2700 and R100 cubes using 1 or 2 Gaussian components.
key_parameters: 1-comp: 20 < σ < 300 km s^-1; 2-comp: 20 < σ_n < 120 km s^-1, 140 < σ_b < 300 km s^-1; 3x3 spaxel averaging
assumptions: [N II]λ6583/[N II]λ6548 and [O III]λ5007/[O III]λ4959 fixed to 2.99; [O II] and [S II] doublet ratios bounded by theoretical limits for 1-10^5 cm^-3

recipe.goal: Derive ISM properties (attenuation, excitation, metallicity, SFR, ionisation parameter, electron density) and outflow energetics
recipe.method: Calculate A_V from Hα/Hβ Balmer decrement, BPT ratios, metallicity from R3/O3O2/R23, SFR from dust-corrected Hα, log U from S2S3, n_e from simultaneous [S II] and [O II] fit, and outflow mass/rate from broad Hα.
assumptions: Intrinsic Hα/Hβ = 2.86 (Case B, T_e = 10^4 K, n_e = 10^2-10^3 cm^-3); Cardelli et al. (1989) attenuation law; Chabrier (2003) IMF; Kennicutt & Evans (2012) SFR relation; Curti et al. (2020b) metallicity calibrations; Sanders et al. (2016) density formulas

The gas-phase metallicity in the main galaxy is 12+log(O/H) = 8.45 ± 0.04

score_reason: JWST NIRSpec spectral fitting, aperture definitions, priors, and physical parameter calibrations are thoroughly documented with complete flux tables in the appendices, though custom JWST pipeline modifications are external and ALMA imaging details are minimal.
rediscovery_reason: Both the JWST (#1216) and ALMA (2012.1.00423.S) datasets are public in archives, aperture coordinates/sizes are tabulated in Table 1, and all derived physical quantities and line fluxes are explicitly reported as numeric answer keys.
